findings.title: Surge of blocked requests (WAF/firewall)
findings.summary: The WAF or firewall blocked more requests than usual; this may be an attack.
findings.help: Review the zone's security events for the source IPs, countries and rules that matched, and check that legitimate users are not blocked.

findings.title: Surge of challenged requests
findings.summary: More requests were challenged (CAPTCHA, JS challenge), often bots or an attack.
findings.help: Review the security events for the rules that matched, and check that real users or API clients are not being challenged.

findings.title: Origin error rate (520-530) at or above 2.0 % (heuristic)
findings.summary: Cloudflare could not reach the origin or got invalid responses (520-530).
findings.help: Check that the origin is up, its firewall allows Cloudflare's IP ranges, TLS certificates are valid and responses are not timing out.

findings.title: Origin response time (p95) above expected range
findings.summary: The origin took longer to respond to Cloudflare for the slowest 5 % of requests.
findings.help: Check the origin's application latency, dependencies and resource saturation.

findings.title: Edge server error rate (5xx) at or above 5.0 % (heuristic)
findings.summary: A larger share of edge responses were 5xx errors.
findings.help: Check whether they come from the origin (520-530 errors, origin logs) or from Cloudflare itself (status page).

findings.title: Edge time to first byte (p95) above expected range
findings.summary: The edge took longer to send the first byte to the slowest 5 % of visitors.
findings.help: Compare with the origin response time: if both rose, the origin is slow; otherwise look at cache hit share and edge routing.
